about: Every tag in a note's text, in order: its frontmatter tags, then the #tags in its body (fenced code and inline code skipped). Duplicates are kept.

cases.name: at line start and after a list marker
digits only is not a tag
needs a space or line start before the #
cases.note: Obsidian likely agrees for a#b and \#f; (#e) unverified.

cases.name: a URL fragment is not a tag
a wikilink heading is not a tag
combining accent (decomposed é)
cases.note: TS stops at U+0301 (a mark, not \p{L}). Obsidian's tag pattern is believed to exclude only whitespace, ASCII punctuation and U+2000-206F / U+2E00-2E7F, so it keeps the mark. Verify.

cases.name: Devanagari vowel signs
cases.note: TS stops at the first vowel sign (Mc/Mn, not \p{L}). Obsidian likely keeps the word whole (see the combining accent case). Verify.

cases.name: emoji
cases.note: TS allows only letters, digits, _ - /. Obsidian likely allows emoji in tags. Verify.

cases.name: CJK full stop
cases.note: U+3002 is outside the ranges Obsidian is believed to exclude. Verify.

cases.name: double-backtick inline code
cases.note: TS blanks single-backtick pairs only (`[^`]*`), so it splits the span at the inner backtick. CommonMark (and so Obsidian, likely) reads ``#a ` #b`` as one code span. Rust's blank_inline_code (links) does it the CommonMark way.

cases.name: a shorter fence does not close a longer one
the other marker does not close a fence
fence indented with a tab is not a fence
cases.note: TS: a fence opens with at most 3 spaces, so a tab-indented ``` is not one. CommonMark agrees (a tab is 4 columns: an indented code line). Rust's fence_open trims any whitespace up to 3 characters, so it opens a fence here (see links.json).

cases.name: fence indented 4 spaces is not a fence
closing fence indented 4 spaces does not close
cases.note: TS and CommonMark: a closing fence has at most 3 spaces of indent, so the block runs on to the end. Rust's fence_close trims any indent and closes here (see links.json).

cases.name: closing fence with text after it does not close
a backtick in a backtick fence's info string: not a fence
unclosed fence runs to the end
indented code block
cases.note: TS has no indented-code-block rule. Obsidian probably does not tag inside an indented code block. Unverified; no obsidian value given.

cases.name: frontmatter YAML comment after the value
frontmatter must start on line 1
cases.note: Frontmatter must start on line 1; here it does not, so the --- block is body text.

cases.name: a # inside frontmatter is not a body tag
BOM before frontmatter
cases.note: TS: frontmatter must start with ---, and a BOM comes first. Rust's parse_note strips a BOM. Obsidian likely reads the frontmatter. Verify.
